newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO, Egypt worried by Israel's Jerusalem plans.
newsitem.headline: PLO, Egypt worried by Israel's Jerusalem plans.

text.p: A Palestinian official blasted on Monday Israeli plans to tighten its grip on disputed Arab East Jerusalem, accusing the Jewish state of putting obstacles to negotiations on the fate of the holy city.
Egypt said Israel's latest plans for East Jerusalem were worrying and could damage the atmosphere in Middle East peace talks.

Israel's ministerial committee on Jerusalem, headed by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, decided on Sunday to allocate $39 million to improve infrastructure in East Jerusalem in a move it said was to strengthen Israeli sovereignty there.

"We are astonished at these decisions," Palestinian President Yasser Arafat's media adviser Nabil Abu Rdainah told Reuters. "These decisions aim at reviving obstacles to negotiations and to preempt final status talks which cover several issues, including the future of Jerusalem."

Moussa said in Cairo: "These reports are worrying and annoying and point to a negative style which will have its effect on the atmosphere, which has begun to improve after implementation of the Hebron agreement."

Israel captured East Jerusalem, holy to Islam, Christianity and Judaism, in the 1967 Middle East war along with the rest of the West Bank and Gaza. Israel says East Jerusalem should remain part of an undivided Israeli capital. The Palestinians want it to be the capital of the independent state they hope to set up.

Under interim Israeli-PLO peace deals that launched Palestinian self-rule in parts of the West Bank and Gaza, the fate of Jerusalem is to be negotiated in "final status" peace talks due to be completed by May 1999.

"Egypt is following this matter closely because Jerusalem is a very delicate subject and should be on the table in the final negotiations between the Palestinians and Israelis," Moussa told reporters.
"Nothing should be done to change the nature, status or demographic structure of the city so that it doesn't damage the negotiations," he said.
About 160,000 Palestinians live in East Jerusalem. An equal number of Jews have settled around the Arab city since 1967.
The Israeli committee said in a statement after it met on Sunday that its decisions were intended to prevent "foreign political and diplomatic activity" in the city.
"The government of Israel will act to strengthen Israeli sovereignty in Jerusalem and for this purpose will allocate the necessary resources," the statement said.
Netanyahu's government says PLO political activity in Jerusalem is illegal and contradicts interim peace deals.
